text:
alex: FYI — wrapping up the bridge notes here. Root cause looks like the autoscaler mis-evaluated GPU utilization and we hit a thread-starve on the realtime pool. Mitigation was to force-scale the pool and fail over traffic to the secondary region.

morgan: thanks. can we capture the immediate action items and a short statuspage blurb? customer wants a concise recap.

jess: putting action list below. will schedule postmortem tomorrow at 11am PT. cc @sre-lead for timeline sign-off.

sre-oncall-bot: Incident #INC-2026-382 acknowledged by alex. Priority: P1. Paging closed at 2026-06-12T18:12:34Z.

alex: immediate actions done during mitigation:
- forced scale realtime-pool by +4 nodes (sam-ops) :white_check_mark:
- rolled traffic to secondary-eu region (deploy-bot) :white_check_mark:
- disabled aggressive autoscaler policy "aggr-scale-v2" (jess) :white_check_mark:
- enabled degraded-mode routing for low-tier customers (morgan) :white_check_mark:

sam-ops: added one-off alert to monitor queue-latency > 200ms for next 24h. I also captured the scaling event logs: `scale_event_id=se-7892` in case we need timeline.

deploy-bot: Rollout job `traffic-shift-eu-2026-06-12` completed. No failed hosts.

morgan: draft status page blurb (short):
"Between 18:02 and 18:10 UTC today we experienced elevated latencies for hosted realtime inference in us-west-2 due to a misconfigured autoscaler. Traffic was shifted to eu-west-1 and normal performance was restored by 18:12 UTC. A full post-incident report and RCA will be published within 72 hours."

amanda-cs: that sounds good. can you add a line about customer impact (who saw errors vs latency)? we need that for our accounts.

jess: good point. updated draft:
"Impact: Customers using the realtime hosted endpoint in us-west-2 experienced increased response latency and intermittent 5xx errors. Lower-tier traffic was routed to degraded mode; no data was lost."

alex: OK. Next: postmortem scheduling and owners. Proposed timeline:
- Postmortem doc created (alex) — due by EOD tomorrow
- Detailed RCA analysis (jess + sre-lead) — draft by +48 hours
- Autoscaler policy audit (sam-ops) — report +72 hours
- Fix: revert to conservative autoscaler thresholds and add canary checks (engineering/runtime) — patch by +7 days

jess: assigning owners inline: RCA owner = jess, autoscaler audit owner = sam-ops, remediation PR owner = alex. I'll create tasks in the incident tracker.

alex: customer comms plan: share status page entry now, then send a customer-facing RCA email to affected accounts once the RCA draft is ready. Amanda, can you coordinate the account outreach?

amanda-cs: yep — I'll prepare a short email template and a list of affected tenants. prefer to wait for RCA draft before sending wide email; we can do targeted pings to top-10 accounts earlier.

morgan: here's a quick targeted email template for top accounts (draft):
```
Hi <Name>,

We wanted to let you know about a service disruption on Jun 12 that affected realtime inference in us-west-2. We shifted traffic to eu-west-1 and restored performance within ~10 minutes. We're investigating the root cause (autoscaler evaluation) and will share a full RCA within 72 hours.

If you saw errors during the window please reply and we'll prioritize a follow-up.

Thanks,
Redwood Support
```

amanda-cs: perfect, I'll personalize and start outreach. will keep the thread updated with any account replies.

sre-lead: a couple of notes for the postmortem:
- include timeline with scale_event_id and autoscaler decision traces (se-7892)
- add a regression test for the autoscaler logic (simulate burst + steady load)
- consider a hard cap that prevents the autoscaler from downscaling below N reserves during high tail latency

jess: adding those. Also proposing these action items with owners and due dates: 
1) Create postmortem doc in /incidents/docs (alex) — due 2026-06-13 23:59 UTC
2) Attach runtime logs and scale traces to doc (sam-ops) — due 2026-06-14 23:59 UTC
3) Draft RCA and mitigation plan (jess) — due 2026-06-15 23:59 UTC
4) Autoscaler policy audit + recommend threshold (sam-ops) — due 2026-06-16 23:59 UTC
5) Implement canary checks and conservative thresholds (eng-runtime / alex) — PR by 2026-06-19
6) Customer-facing RCA and outreach (amanda-cs) — send after RCA draft is reviewed by sre-lead

alex: I'll create the doc now and link it here. Also adding a quick post-incident checklist for trust recovery:
- publish status page entry (morgan) — now
- targeted account pings for top-10 (amanda-cs) — within 2 hours
- public RCA in 72 hours (jess)
- follow-up meeting with product + security for risk review (sre-lead) — within 1 week

morgan: status page entry posted: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/1911112222 — please review and thumbs if okay :thumbsup:

alex: thumbs.

amanda-cs: two account replies already; both saw latency but no data loss. I'll paste notes into the doc.

sam-ops: putting link to scale logs in the postmortem doc and flagging an interesting anomaly where the autoscaler sampled a stale metric window. Investigating metric pipeline delays.

jess: capturing follow-ups in the tracker. tagging `eng-runtime` and `metrics-team` for the metric-window issue.

sre-oncall-bot: On-call handoff: alex -> jess at 2026-06-13T08:00Z.

alex: thanks. I'll do a quick handover note in the doc summarizing current mitigations and short-term watch items (alerts >= 200ms, queue depth > 50).

morgan: thanks everyone. let's keep updates brief here. next check-in after RCA draft. :raised_hands:

jess: will post the postmortem link and action checklist once doc is created.

deploy-bot: Notification: `traffic-shift-eu-2026-06-12` archived to `incidents/archives/1911112222`.

alex: closing the bridge. leaving this thread open for follow-ups and account notes."
